description.p: Big Game Mode is the gaming centre of BigLinux. Turbo switches falcond on, so every game gets its performance profile, applied when it starts and undone when it closes. Big Game Mode shows what is really in effect, measures whether a change helped, and manages upscaling and frame generation inside games, with full backup and undo.

ul.li: Turbo: one switch for per-game optimization through falcond
Profiles for Steam, Lutris, Heroic and native games, offered when an unknown game starts
AI Graphics: OptiScaler installed with verified backups, repair and restore
Measure the difference: repeated A/B runs with a statistical verdict
Real-time telemetry, diagnostics and one view of every relevant log
Stays in the tray when the window is closed

description.p: Processors without AVX2, such as Sandy Bridge and Ivy Bridge: when the installed falcond cannot run on them, Turbo still comes on with the general settings, says why, and does not start that falcond again until the package changes.

ul.li: A falcond that crashes at start no longer stays enabled to crash again at every boot, and Turbo can be turned off after it
The Steam runtime's library cache tool is no longer taken for the running game

description.p: The product is now called Big Game Mode. The tray is a quick control with Turbo, the four presets and its own symbolic icon. Steam, Heroic and Lutris opened before a preset can be reopened from a notice. A profile can be started from its editor with Turbo. Home names the CPU and every GPU on any machine.

ul.li: lsfg-vk 2.x: its configuration format is read and written, and a Lossless.dll it cannot use is reported instead of breaking the game
Hybrid NVIDIA laptops: Gamescope no longer crashes, and nested Gamescope shows the game the screen's size
Turbo rolls back cleanly when falcond fails to start, and presets leave nothing behind when switched off
Faster, more accurate game detection for Steam, Heroic and Lutris
AI Graphics: frame generation shown active only when OptiScaler's log proves it, safer Restore and Repair, and a download cache that keeps only the releases games use
A stricter privileged helper, and about 0.15 % of a CPU core when idle in the tray
No extra repository needed: falcond, lsfg-vk, sched-ext, Gamescope, MangoHud and vkBasalt are optional, and what needs one says so and how to install it

description.p: A welcome screen, a rewritten About and Help; Tuning with Gamescope always in view, standard resolutions and the main screen's size, and vkBasalt looks (CAS or the Nara Linux style); game profiles with the same rows as Tuning, reaching Steam and Heroic games; Launch (Turbo) through every launcher and Reopen for one opened before the preset; a redesigned AI Graphics window that follows a game's launcher stub and sees upscalers built into the executable; background programs can be closed or paused, a measured DNS applied with a backup, and falcond handed back and taken again.

Turbo presets chosen before switching it on (More FPS, Locked 60 FPS, Enhanced graphics), a redrawn Home with a power button, live readings and the running game's features as coloured flags; Tuning, game profiles and the profile wizard on one model, with every conflict asked; Gamescope and Wine FSR reach Steam games through their launch options; launchers are no longer taken for the game; Details tells when falcond does not apply a game's profile, and why.

Six pages, with Details showing what is really in effect and the evidence for it; AI Graphics raises FSR 3.1 to FSR 4 through Proton and finds the upscalers Unreal Engine games ship as plugins; MangoHud per game for Steam, Heroic and Lutris; the Gamer theme; every text translated into 29 languages; a stricter sandbox for the privileged helper.

Turbo as the master switch over falcond, per-game profiles offered when an unknown game starts, AI Graphics with OptiScaler (backup, repair and restore), a benchmark lab with A/B verdicts, diagnostics and a unified log view.
Initial release with dashboard, profiles, tuning, and gamescope panels.
